newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand tightens problem loan disclosure norms.
newsitem.headline: Thailand tightens problem loan disclosure norms.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday announced measures tightening disclosure norms for non-performing loans of financial institutions.

Senior central bank official Nongnaj Sondhisuwan said commercial banks and finance companies would be required this year to detail all non-performing loans when they issued half-year financial statements.
She said non-bank finance companies would have to break down accrued interest figures by sectors as part of a central bank policy to standardise public disclosure of problem loans.
"The central bank, under the leadership of Governor Rerngchai Marakanond, wants to see the financial sector conduct business in a more transparent manner," Nongnaj said.

"Management of financial institutions should not try to dress up balance sheets. We want to see proper business ethics and professionalism in this sector which should appreciate that they are managing public savings."
Market analysts said a prolonged slump in the Thai property sector had increased non-performing loans carried by Thai banks and finance companies in the past year.
Central bank officials said non-performing and doubtful loans carried by Thai banks in mid-1996 amounted on average to 7.73 percent of outstanding credit.
Nongnaj said the new measures fine-tuned existing disclosure rules on non-performing loans which would help curb attempts to cover up problem loans handled by financial institutions.

The measures called for financial institutions to detail non-performing collateralised loans that are not serviced for more than 12 months and itemise uncollateralised loans defaulted on for more than six months.
